title: Compact GPU dependency index and deterministic init path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over the last 18 months we accumulated a broad set of heterogeneous GPU dependency heuristics (multiple manifest formats, duplicated symbol resolution paths, and runtime probe fallbacks). This causes nondeterministic init latency, high cold-start jitter, and makes safe kernel upgrades difficult. Goal: build a compact, single-source GPU dependency index and a deterministic init sequence that reduces probe jitter, shrinks the runtime's dynamic linker surface, and provides an atomic upgrade/rollback path for CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA artifacts. The work should be non-invasive for hosted customers and behind a feature flag for Dedicated/Private environments.
acceptance_criteria: Single flat dependency index produced at build-time (json manifest) consumed by runtime loader
Cold-start kernel probe 95th percentile latency reduced by >=50% on representative p4/p5 machines
Deterministic init path with timeout-safeguards and a verified rollback path for failed kernel activation
Automated CI gated canary: bundle validation job that verifies symbol set and launches smoke runtime in hermetic container
No regression in existing functional tests; new integration tests added that exercise heterogeneous-device fallback and mixed-quant kernels
implementation_steps: Design manifest schema (flat index referencing kernel bundles, ABI fingerprint, and CPU-side heuristics) - draft in confluence
Introduce build-time generator that aggregates CUTLASS / triton plugin / cuda provider metadata into compact index
Replace runtime probe discovery with index-driven resolver; make probe timeboxed and observable
Add deliberate deterministic ordering for kernel activation (by ABI stability score, fallback rank)
Wire in atomic activation transaction: provision -> validate symbols -> swap pointer table -> commit or rollback
Feature flag and gradual rollout: enable on staging, run canary fleet, then enable for Dedicated customers by opt-in
Add CI checks and preflight validation (bundle signature verification + symbol diffing)
Documentation and runbook for operator-triggered rollbacks and emergency disables
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal staging build with feature flag enabled; smoke on 3 node types (p4, a100-small, rtx6000) - 2 weeks
Phase 1: Canary on small subset of Hosted (non-critical) traffic with telemetry checks - 1 week
Phase 2: Open rollout to Dedicated customers as opt-in (support ticket + release notes) - 2 weeks
Phase 3: Auto-enable for remaining infra if telemetry stable for 7 days; monitor error budget and latency SLOs
Rollback: flip feature flag and invoke atomic rollback path which reverts pointer tables and invalidates new bundles
testing_plan: Unit tests for index generator and manifest parser
Integration test: launch runtime in hermetic container with mixed kernels and validate KV cache behavior
Performance regression suite measuring init latency percentiles across machine classes
Canary validation job (GitHub Actions) that verifies bundle signature and attempts dry-run activation
Chaos test: simulate missing symbol and ensure deterministic fallback route is exercised and logged
notes: Avoid introducing a second runtime lookup path; the goal is to converge existing discovery logic into a single resolver
We must preserve backwards compatibility with older runtime images that still expect the legacy manifest. Plan to emit both formats for one release and deprecate legacy in follow-ups
Quant kernels require special handling: include quant-profile tag in index so runtime chooses quant-friendly kernels when allowed
Tie telemetry to existing cost/latency dashboards (console-2025.08) so SRE can set alerts on probe regressions
Consider binary diff artifacts to reduce network push size when releasing new kernel bundles to Dedicated customers

2025-11-21 — Carlos Nguyen: landed generator + parser in feature branch. Added timebox to probe loop (default 200ms) and fallback rank ordering. Running perf runs; 95p init latency down to 180ms on p4 (optimistic).
